transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

Not necessarily. Damp laundry after a combined wash-and-dry programme is more often caused by putting a full wash load straight into drying, a short/low dryness setting, or a restriction in the drying/condensing path than by the heater itself. A washer-dryer usually dries substantially less than it can wash, so a load that washes successfully may need splitting before drying. The useful divider is heat: if the drum or clothes are noticeably warm but still damp, the heater is likely working and the issue is more likely load size, settings, airflow/condensing or drainage. If everything remains cold through the drying stage, a heater, thermal cut-out, fan or control fault becomes more likely. Was the load split to within the stated dry capacity, and did it feel warm at the end?
No, I haven't split it - I put a full 9kg drum in and it washes and dries in one go. The manual says 6kg for drying. And yes, at the end the clothes are hot but still damp.

The heater is very unlikely to be the problem: hot clothes show that it is producing heat. A 9 kg wash load is over the 6 kg drying limit, so there is too much wet fabric in the drum for the moisture to be condensed and pumped away in the drying time; damp-but-hot laundry is the expected result rather than evidence of a failed part. Split the wash into two drying loads of 6 kg maximum (slightly under is better), and use a full drying programme rather than a short timed option. If a reduced load is still hot and remains damp, the next likely causes are the cold-water supply/condensing route or a drain restriction, rather than the heater.

candidates: Drying load exceeds the appliance's dry capacity or drying setting is too low/short (high)
Restricted drying airflow/condensing path or pump filter restriction (medium)
Drying heater, thermostat, fan or control fault (medium)
